notes: Read by the workflow and by the eval harness, and interpreted only by workflows/code/route.js, so the two cannot route differently.
The contract is what validate-classification.js holds model output to. Output that fails it is CLASSIFICATION_FAILED and never reaches these rules.
Rules are tried in order; the first whose conditions all hold wins. Conditions compare `relevance` or `criteria.<name>` for equality and are ANDed.

Order is load-bearing. `contradiction` must precede `not-relevant`, or output that calls a notice irrelevant while its own criteria say it is software in the target market would be dismissed with no human seeing it (docs/DESIGN-AMENDMENTS.md A2). It precedes the other review rules too, so a contradiction is always labelled as one.
`scope-unclear` precedes `not-relevant`, as in the design doc: an irrelevant verdict with unclear scope goes to review. Over-review is the safe direction.
`strong-match` requires all four criteria (A6). A rule may route to AUTO_MATCH or NOT_RELEVANT only when it requires the matching verdict; route.js refuses this file otherwise.
Anything no rule matches falls back to NEEDS_REVIEW. Confidence appears in no rule: it is not calibrated and routes nothing.
